_help: Editable config for ScrapeX (scrapex.py). Add accounts or search queries to the lists below and save; the next run picks them up. JSON has no comments, so keep the structure (commas, quotes, brackets) intact. Handles go WITHOUT the leading @. When in doubt, ask Claude to edit it for you.
_accounts_help: X accounts whose timelines we read every run. These are the paper-discovery accounts — when they post a paper, that paper is on the radar. 'role' is a note for you, not used by the code. Retweets count: if one of these accounts RTs a paper post, we take the ORIGINAL post's metrics and record who surfaced it.
_search_help: Full-site X searches, run after the account timelines. This is how papers reach us from accounts NOT on the list above ('and many more'). These are raw X search strings — every X search operator works: min_faves:N, min_retweets:N, -filter:replies, since:YYYY-MM-DD, lang:en. Raise the min_faves numbers if a run returns too much noise.
search_queries: ("new paper" OR "our paper" OR "paper drop") arxiv min_faves:400 -filter:replies lang:en
_weights_help: How a post's reach turns into a number. views measures exposure; engagement measures whether anyone actually cared, so engagement is multiplied up to sit on the same scale as views (engagement typically runs 1-2% of views). Retweets/quotes/bookmarks are weighted above likes because they cost the reader more. Edit these to retune what floats to the top.
_settings_help: tweets_per_account / tweets_per_query bound how much each source pulls per run. min_reach_to_report is the floor a paper must clear before it shows up in the report at all (it is still stored). climb_threshold is how much a paper's reach must GROW, as a fraction, before an already-reported paper resurfaces in the 'still climbing' section — 0.5 means it needs +50%. request_delay_seconds spaces out calls so X does not rate-limit the run.
_rate_limit_help: X rate-limits hard, and the limit is per account across a rolling window — not per run. Each account costs a lookup plus one request per page of tweets, so 11 accounts at 25 tweets is roughly 25-30 requests before the searches even start. Symptoms of being throttled: 'X rate-limited us' on timelines, and searches quietly returning 0 tweets (X answers SearchTimeline with a 404 rather than a 429 when it is throttling you). The fix is always to wait, not to retry — this is meant to be run about once a day, which comfortably fits the budget.
